There are several passages in this test.
Each passage is followed by several questions. After
reading a passage, choose the best answer to each
question and fill in the corresponding oval on your
answer document. You may refer to the passages as
permitted to use a calculator on this test.
GO ON TO THE NEXT PAGE.
Oil leaked into the soil can increase the concentration
of heavy metals in soil, resulting in soil pollution. Plants
can help mitigate this pollution by absorbing heavy metals
from the soil. Table 1 shows, for each of 2 kinds of plants
(maize and cowpeas) planted in either unpolluted soil or in
oil-polluted soil, the average concentrations, in parts per
million (ppm), for each of 5 heavy metals contained in the
plants at the end of 6 weeks of growth.
